info.name: Break Journey Tracker API
info.description:
Postman collection for the `break-journey-tracker` Spring Boot project (Kolkata to Hyderabad, 23-24 Nov 2026).

## Before you start
1. Start the app: `mvn spring-boot:run` (port 8080).
2. Import this collection **and** `Break-Journey-Tracker.postman_environment.json`, then select the environment *Break Journey Tracker - Local*.
3. Run folders **in order (0 to 6)**. You can use the Collection Runner (Run collection) to execute everything; the tests assert expected values.
4. Optional: keep http://localhost:8080/ open to watch live SSE updates while you send requests.

## Delay model in one paragraph
Train and bus run to the timetable plus their reported delay. Cab/auto legs leave at the later of their planned time and the previous leg's arrival plus a 10 minute handoff. Buffer = bus departure minus arrival at Baramunda. Risk: >= 40 min SAFE, 15-39 TIGHT_CONNECTION, < 15 CRITICAL_MISSED_CONNECTION. The delay you send is the **total** delay (it replaces the old value; 0 clears it).

## Collection variables
`baseUrl` (default http://localhost:8080) and `journeyId` (set automatically by request 0.1; seeded journey is `1`).

item.name: 0. Smoke test and setup
item.description: Confirms the app is running, the data is seeded, and captures the journey id into `journeyId`.

request.description:
**Goal:** Verify startup seeding (`DataInitializer`) and store the id.

**Steps:**
1. Send the request.
2. Expect 200 and exactly one journey for Souptik Tat with 4 legs.
3. The test script saves `journeyId` as a collection variable used by every other request.

exec: pm.test("Passenger is Souptik Tat, 34, Male", () => { pm.expect(j.passenger.name).to.eql("Souptik Tat"); pm.expect(j.passenger.age).to.eql(34); pm.expect(j.passenger.gender).to.eql("Male"); pm.expect(j.passenger.contactNumber).to.eql("+919038577517"); });
pm.test("Four legs in order CAB, TRAIN, AUTO_CAB, BUS", () => pm.expect(j.legs.map(l => l.mode)).to.eql(["CAB","TRAIN","AUTO_CAB","BUS"]));

request.description:
**Goal:** Stop any simulation, clear all delays and set every leg to SCHEDULED. Run this before each scenario folder if a previous test left delays behind.

**Steps:** Send the request; expect 200 with `running: false`.

item.name: 1. Read journey details
item.description: Verifies every itinerary detail you seeded: PNRs, seats, times, fare and the baseline 50 minute buffer.

request.description:
**Goal:** Check the complete seeded itinerary.

**Steps:** Send; review the tests. They verify leg 1 (cab, 11.7 km), leg 2 (PNR 6951647716, txn 100006932256103, Coach C6 seat 78), leg 3 (7.7 km, 50 min layover) and leg 4 (ticket TVBQ22662970, PNR 7296768, seat K1, INR 1568.05).

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); const L = j.legs;
pm.test("Journey title", () => pm.expect(j.title).to.include("Kolkata to Hyderabad Break Journey"));

pm.test("Leg 1 cab details", () => { pm.expect(L[0].distanceKm).to.eql(11.7); pm.expect(L[0].origin).to.include("Xclusive Mansion"); pm.expect(new Date(L[0].recommendedBookingTime).getTime()).to.eql(new Date("2026-11-23T04:15:00+05:30").getTime()); });

pm.test("Leg 2 train bookings", () => { pm.expect(L[1].operatorName).to.eql("22895 Howrah - Puri Vande Bharat Express"); pm.expect(L[1].bookingReference).to.eql("6951647716"); pm.expect(L[1].transactionId).to.eql("100006932256103"); pm.expect(L[1].seatInfo).to.include("Coach C6"); pm.expect(L[1].distanceKm).to.eql(436); pm.expect(L[1].expectedDelayBufferMinutes).to.eql(30); });

pm.test("Leg 4 bus bookings", () => { pm.expect(L[3].operatorName).to.eql("Shyamoli Paribahan Pvt Ltd"); pm.expect(L[3].ticketNumber).to.eql("TVBQ22662970"); pm.expect(L[3].bookingReference).to.eql("7296768"); pm.expect(L[3].seatNumber).to.eql("K1"); pm.expect(Number(L[3].fare)).to.eql(1568.05); pm.expect(L[3].currency).to.eql("INR"); });
pm.test("Bus arrives Miyapur 24 Nov 08:30 IST", () => pm.expect(new Date(L[3].scheduledArrival).getTime()).to.eql(new Date("2026-11-24T08:30:00+05:30").getTime()));

item.name: 2. Vande Bharat delay scenarios (ripple effect)
item.description: Core feature. Each request **sets** the total delay on leg 2 and checks Bhubaneswar arrival, auto departure, Baramunda arrival, buffer and risk. Run in order. If you re-run a single request, run 0.2 first.

request.description:
**Goal:** Report that the Vande Bharat (leg 2) is 30 minutes late.

**Expected ripple:**
- Arrives Bhubaneswar 11:58
- Auto/cab leaves 12:10
- Reaches Baramunda 12:40
- Buffer before 13:30 bus: 50 min
- Risk: SAFE

The 30 minute delay is absorbed by the gap between train arrival and the planned auto departure, so the buffer does not shrink.

**Steps:**
1. Make sure *Reset* was run (folder 1) so no earlier delay is left.
2. Send the request.
3. Open the *Test Results* tab; all tests should pass.
4. (Optional) Open http://localhost:8080/ in a browser first and watch the alert banner and buffer card change live.

**Goal:** Report that the Vande Bharat (leg 2) is 50 minutes late.

**Expected ripple:**
- Arrives Bhubaneswar 12:18
- Auto/cab leaves 12:28
- Reaches Baramunda 12:58
- Buffer before 13:30 bus: 32 min
- Risk: TIGHT_CONNECTION

Buffer drops below 40 min, so the risk becomes TIGHT_CONNECTION.

**Steps:**
1. Make sure *Reset* was run (folder 1) so no earlier delay is left.
2. Send the request.
3. Open the *Test Results* tab; all tests should pass.
4. (Optional) Open http://localhost:8080/ in a browser first and watch the alert banner and buffer card change live.

Only 17 minutes remain. Check the recommendations: pre-book the auto, skip lunch, message the operator.

**Steps:**
1. Make sure *Reset* was run (folder 1) so no earlier delay is left.
2. Send the request.
3. Open the *Test Results* tab; all tests should pass.
4. (Optional) Open http://localhost:8080/ in a browser first and watch the alert banner and buffer card change live.

**Goal:** Report that the Vande Bharat (leg 2) is 70 minutes late.

**Expected ripple:**

- Auto/cab leaves 12:48
- Reaches Baramunda 13:18
- Buffer before 13:30 bus: 12 min

**Steps:**

item.name: 3. Threshold boundaries
item.description: Proves the exact cut-offs: 40 min is SAFE, 39 is TIGHT, 15 is TIGHT, 14 is CRITICAL.

request.description: Threshold check. A 42 minute train delay gives a 40 minute buffer, which must be **SAFE**.
Threshold check. A 43 minute train delay gives a 39 minute buffer, which must be **TIGHT_CONNECTION**.
Threshold check. A 67 minute train delay gives a 15 minute buffer, which must be **TIGHT_CONNECTION**.
Threshold check. A 68 minute train delay gives a 14 minute buffer, which must be **CRITICAL_MISSED_CONNECTION**.
Reset delays before the next folder.

item.name: 4. Delays on other legs and status updates
item.description: Shows the ripple works on any leg, and manual status changes.

item.name: 4.1 Cab to Howrah +70 min (train boarding at risk)

request.description:
**Goal:** A late cab eats the buffer before the 06:10 train.

**Expected:** cab arrives 06:10, train leaves 06:10, so the cab-to-train buffer is 0 and the overall risk is CRITICAL.
Clear the cab delay (0).

**Goal:** Manual status change. Overall journey should become IN_PROGRESS.

Allowed values: SCHEDULED, IN_TRANSIT, DELAYED, COMPLETED.
Complete the cab leg.
Reset statuses and delays.

item.name: 5. Live simulation
item.description: Runs the accelerated simulation (default 600x: 10 virtual minutes per real second, about 170 seconds for the whole journey). Tip: open http://localhost:8080/ in a browser first to watch it.

request.description:
**Steps:** Send; expect running true. The virtual clock starts at 04:00 on 23 Nov.

**Optional:** Before sending, run 2.3 (+65 min) to see the simulation play out a tight connection.
**Steps:** Send several times, a few seconds apart. `virtualTime` should keep advancing. When `finished` becomes true the journey is complete (about 3 minutes).
**Steps:** Send while the simulation runs. Leg statuses follow the virtual clock (SCHEDULED, then IN_TRANSIT, then COMPLETED). After it finishes, all legs are COMPLETED and the journey is COMPLETED.
Stops the simulation and returns everything to SCHEDULED.
All legs back to SCHEDULED, delays 0, journey SCHEDULED.

item.name: 7. Live stream (SSE)
item.description: Server-Sent Events are easiest to observe outside the normal Postman request tab.

request.description:
**Event types:** `snapshot` (progress, active leg, ETAs, buffer, risk) and `alert` (human readable notices).

**How to test (pick one):**
1. **Browser dashboard:** open http://localhost:8080/ (it uses this stream).
2. **curl:** `curl -N http://localhost:8080/api/v1/journeys/1/live-stream` in a terminal, then send requests 2.1 to 2.5 or 5.1 from Postman. You should see an `alert` and a new `snapshot` for every change, plus a snapshot every 5 seconds.
3. **Postman:** this request may be opened as a plain HTTP request; the response streams, so use *Cancel* once you have seen the first events. Newer Postman versions can show it as an event stream.

**Expected:** first event is a `snapshot` sent immediately on connect.
